title: Adam Robinson's 8 SaaS marketing strategies that work: founder brand, inbound-led outbound, UGC, word of mouth
summary: Adam Robinson, who has scaled three SaaS companies to 35M combined ARR, walks through eight marketing strategies he uses at RB2B: founder brand, inbound-led outbound, cold email, LinkedIn DMs, paid ads as an accelerator, UGC, and word of mouth. His core argument is that product-market fit and word of mouth come first, and every other tactic only works well once you have them.

principles.text: Build a founder brand by being vulnerable and clear about who you are; big companies can't copy that.
principles.quote: Be incredibly clear about who you are. For me, it's a bootstrapped SAS founder who builds in public.

principles.text: Content is the ultimate leverage: it drives inbound leads at almost no cost beyond your time.
principles.quote: As a founder, you need to realize that content is the ultimate leverage.

principles.text: Combine inbound and outbound: drive traffic, identify ICP visitors, then follow up with them like warm prospects.
principles.quote: They've already shown intent by visiting your website. Our conversion rates are 10 times higher than traditional cold outreach.

principles.text: Cold email at volume works only with a clean list: pull from multiple data sources, verify every email, and rotate many sending domains.
principles.quote: Don't just use one tool, use five or six. And always validate your emails before sending.

principles.text: On LinkedIn, run connect, then value, then follow-up: no pitch in the connection request, and stop after three follow-ups.
principles.quote: The goal here is just to get the connection, not to book a meeting.

principles.text: Paid ads are an accelerator, not a foundation; use them to retarget engaged people and ABM lists, with authentic selfie-video creatives.
principles.quote: They're an accelerator. They're not the foundation. You need other things working for you first before ads will be effective at all.
